name: Definisse

card.summary: Definisse is a brand of absorbable barbed suspension threads placed under the skin to lift and reshape the midface, cheeks and jawline without surgery.
card.aka: Happy Lift; Korean HA filler (as the name is sometimes listed)
card.note: Practitioner skill and thread type matter; complications are reported with thread lifts generally.

quick.overview:
Definisse is a thread-lift product made by RELIFE S.r.l. of Florence, Italy. Its double-needle threads have barbs that grip tissue and are made of a copolymer of polycaprolactone and L-lactic acid, which is absorbed over time.[1][6] Clinicians place them to lift cheeks and sharpen the jawline, and they are marketed as a non-surgical option.

Published work is mainly retrospective and observational: studies in Thai, Indian, Hong Kong and other Asian patients report improved aesthetic scores on physician and patient scales at follow-ups up to 12 months. Although it is sometimes listed as a filler, the sources describe Definisse as a thread, not hyaluronic acid.
quick.how: A trained practitioner places threads through the skin along planned vectors for midface, malar or jawline reshaping. Studies describe combining techniques, and one case report combined threads with ultrasound and hyaluronic acid filler.[2] Results are described as immediate with further effects as the body responds to the threads.
quick.risks: Thread lifts in general are described as carrying risks including infection and vessel puncture, and a physician quoted by Wikipedia called non-absorbable threads potentially irreversible; Definisse is absorbable. The studies reviewed reported no major complications, but samples were small and mostly uncontrolled.

lead: Definisse is a brand of bioabsorbable barbed suspension threads for facial lifting, described as fourth-generation threads made by RELIFE S.r.l. in Florence, Italy.[6] The threads are double-needle with convergent bidirectional barbs, made of a poly-epsilon-caprolactone-co-L-lactic acid copolymer.[1][7] The product is also marketed as Happy Lift.[5]

People use it to lift sagging tissue and reshape the face: increasing anterior cheek projection, redefining the jawline, and slimming the lower face, particularly in Asian patients who often seek these effects.[4][5] Sources describe an immediate mechanical lift followed by a biostimulatory effect with collagen and elastin synthesis.[6]

A consensus by the Board of Aesthetic Leaders and Investigators (BALI) describes technique for Asian and Caucasian patients, and observational studies report improved scores at follow-up.[1][3][5][6][7]

chain: Immediate lift of cheek and jaw soft tissue, then collagen response
More defined cheekbones and jawline, slimmer lower face
angle.text: Clinicians place Definisse threads to lift and reposition facial soft tissue for a more contoured jawline and cheeks. Patients and physicians in observational studies rated appearance as improved over months.

infobox: Subcutaneous placement by a trained practitioner

paras: The threads are double-needle monofilaments with convergent bidirectional barbs that suspend tissue; the polymer is absorbed over time.[1][7]
Sources describe a dual action: a mechanical lift followed by stimulation of fibroblasts and production of elastin, hyaluronic acid and collagen.[6]

Studies describe use for midface reshaping, malar reshaping and jawline contouring.[3][4][5][7] The BALI consensus described technique and pre-treatment recommendations for rejuvenation in Asian and Caucasian patients.[1]

A 2023 case report described a sequence of ultrasound-based lower face debulking, Definisse threads and hyaluronic acid filler for jawline contour, with improvement at six months and no major adverse events.[2]

A retrospective study of 60 patients (mean age 51.3, 90 percent female) treated for mid-face reshaping found improved Mid-Face Volume Deficit and FACE-Q scores at six months and no major complications.[3]
A prospective study of 20 Asian patients in Hong Kong using malar reshaping reported marked improvement on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale and a slimmer-looking face.[4]
A blinded prospective study of 27 Thai patients with lower face threads reported immediate improvement in laxity and measured volume changes over 12 months.[5]

The REDEFINE FACE study of 317 Indian patients with mean follow-up of 4.9 months and the REDEFINE JAW study reported improvement on physician and subject scales in real-world use.[6][7] These designs are retrospective or lack control groups.

Wikipedia notes that thread lifts in general have drawn concerns about practitioner training, infection control and vessel puncture, and quotes physician Vincent Wong describing them as potentially irreversible for non-absorbable threads.[8]

timeline.event: BALI panel convenes in Indonesia to develop consensus on Definisse threads.[1]
Studies in Hong Kong and Thai patients published.[4][5]
REDEFINE JAW and REDEFINE FACE real-world studies in India.[6][7]
